comparator.route: Ordinary three-year Dentistry bachelor including preclinical and supervised patient treatment
comparator.sourceNotes: The official year pages itemize 60+60+60=180 EC. Year one consists of 60 EC compulsory orientation, academic/professional formation, dental knowledge, medical–dental interaction and two preclinical dental components. Year two has 57 EC compulsory professional formation, dental knowledge, medical–dental interaction, preclinical training and the 7-EC Bachelor Clinic, plus a genuinely unrestricted 3-EC elective. Radboud specifies supervised patient treatment beginning in the second semester. Year three has 60 EC compulsory academic/professional and research work, dental knowledge, medical–dental interaction, preclinical training, an 11-EC third-year clinic and pain. The year-three page says students work on a bachelor thesis, and itemizes a 10.5-EC research/formation component but no separate thesis line; no additional thesis credits have been invented. The publicly listed year pages do not identify a prospective academic year and should not be treated as a fixed entrant-cohort contract.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Dentistry bachelor; its official three-year year pages give one ordinary 180-EC route. Only the genuinely open 3-EC year-two choice is left unfilled.

exception.reason: The defining curriculum is dental education with successive preclinical dentistry courses across all three years, dental knowledge and medical–dental interaction every year, supervised patient treatment beginning in year two (7 EC) and continuing in year three (11 EC), and dental research/professional formation. Of 180 EC, only a 3-EC year-two choice is unrestricted. UCR does not teach dentistry, dental simulation/preclinical procedures, restorative or oral clinical methods, or supervised treatment in a dental clinic. A 24-course programme in biomedical sciences, anatomy, psychology and health policy would omit the clinical and professional core.
exception.curriculumContext: The official pages reconcile to 180 EC: 60 fully specified compulsory in year one, 57 compulsory plus 3 free EC in year two, and 60 compulsory in year three. The bachelor thesis is described as part of the third year but not separately credited beyond the published research/formation unit; it is not added again. The clinical units are required dental-patient training rather than ordinary internships.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR course rows, including their descriptions, profiles, topics, prerequisites and planned terms. HCBGATE101, HCBLIFE211/212/213/214, HCBBIOM211/311/312/313 and HCBLIFE311 cover biomedical foundations, physiology, anatomy, biochemistry, laboratory methods, pharmacology, infection and disease; HCBBIOM111 and HCBPSYC211 offer health research/statistical methods; HCBPSYC311 adds health psychology. These are relevant adjacent academic perspectives but none teaches tooth and oral-system examination, dental materials and restorative treatment, sequential preclinical dental technical skills or supervised real-patient dental care. No combination of the 151 courses provides an honest 24-course Dentistry comparison.
